what: Whether a clear `2ch_control_enabled` is what makes Dolby's TrueHD object path refuse a stream. Asked by authoring the stimulus with Dolby's own encoder instead of editing a finished stream, which is the instrument that failed
why_this_and_not_a_mutation: the flag correlates perfectly across six titles: set in the three Dolby opens, clear in the three it refuses. Clearing it in every major sync of an accepted title makes Dolby refuse -- but so does changing a dynamic-range gain, and so does changing the two-channel presentation's dialogue normalisation, neither of which can gate the sixteen-channel presentation. The object path reads an edited major sync far more strictly than ordinary decoding does, so a refusal after an edit says little about the field edited. An encoder writing the stream itself has no such problem

the_knob.found: `encode_to_dthd/presentation_2ch/drc_default_on`. With it false, DEE writes `2ch_control_enabled` clear

how_clean_the_pair_is.material: the controlled scene authored here, encoded twice by DEE from the same master
how_clean_the_pair_is.oadec_info_differs_in: one line: `2ch true` becomes `2ch false`. Nothing else, including the file length
how_clean_the_pair_is.where: 100 major syncs contribute one byte each at offset +18 -- the byte the field-level difference table already named as the only whole byte separating the accepted titles from the refused -- and two bytes of recomputed CRC-16 twelve bytes later. The remaining 28 clusters are the two-channel presentation's own DRC data, which is what the option controls
how_clean_the_pair_is.object_audio: byte-identical. `decode -p 3 --format pcm` gives the same 23 040 000 bytes from both, so nothing the object programme carries changed

positive_control.why: an experiment whose every arm is accepted has to show that the instrument can still say no, or `accepted` might only mean `the pipeline did not run`
positive_control.run: the same command, the same session, on the library titles

reading: a clear `2ch_control_enabled` is **not sufficient** to make Dolby's object path refuse. A stream with the flag clear, written legally by Dolby's own encoder, with object audio byte-identical to the accepted control, is opened. The six-title correlation is untouched and so is the possibility that the flag matters in combination with something else, but the flag on its own is now ruled out as the cause
and_it_explains_the_mutation: clearing the flag by hand made Dolby refuse; clearing it at the encoder does not. So the refusal after the hand edit came from the edit, not from the field -- which is what the dynamic-range gain control suggested and this settles. The report's `suggestive but unclean` becomes `not sufficient`
what_stays_open: why Dolby refuses those three titles. Nothing in the 74 fields oadec reports separates the sets, a third-party conformance checker finds nothing that separates them either -- `truehdd verify` gives Shaun and Kingsman DRC warnings, Knives Out none, and Talk to Me the same warnings while being accepted -- and the one byte that did separate them is now shown not to be the cause
